title: js-rag-streaming-walkthrough-and-local-emulator-quickstart
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Add JavaScript streaming RAG quickstart that demonstrates local vector-store emulator, streaming token response handling, tool-calling example, and a tiny e2e smoke test. No breaking changes.
description:
Context: This PR adds a new JavaScript-focused quickstart that demonstrates a streaming RAG pattern end-to-end against a local vector-store emulator. Motivation: many customers want a minimal runnable example that shows (1) ingesting documents, (2) async retrieval, (3) streaming generation with partial tokens, and (4) invoking a simple tool (a URL fetcher) from an agent. Prior examples either used server-side Python or relied on hosted vector services; this doc is targeted at front-end + full-stack engineers who want to iterate locally before provisioning Dedicated/Private resources.

What this PR contains (summary):
- A new quickstart under quickstarts/js-streaming-rag/ with a README walkthrough (step-by-step).
- A lightweight vector-store emulator (emulator/vectorstore-sim.js) that stores embeddings in-memory and exposes a simple HTTP ingest/retrieve API for local testing.
- A streaming agent sample (agent/streaming-agent.js) that demonstrates Redwood API streaming responses, incremental context assembly, and a small tool-calling hook that fetches external URLs safely.
- A small E2E smoke test (test/e2e-emulator-smoke.js) using node-fetch and a mocked Redwood API response to validate the streaming handler and retrieval loop.
- Docs site update: quickstarts index updated (site/content/quickstarts/index.md) with cross-links to the new JS walkthrough.

Checklist: 
- [x] Quickstart README with prerequisites and commands
- [x] Example code (agent + emulator) packaged and runnable with npm install + npm run start
- [x] Minimal E2E smoke test included in test/ and run by CI job quickstart-smoke
- [x] Docs site index entry and sidebar update
- [x] Reviewed and approved by two engineers, security scan passed for local emulator

High-level commits: 
- 8e7b2f0 add quickstart skeleton and README
- 1c4a9b3 implement in-memory vector-store emulator and API shim
- 3b2d5f1 add streaming agent example and tool-calling demo
- 9f0d7a8 add e2e smoke test and CI job for quickstarts
- f1a0c21 docs: add quickstart index entry and cross-links

Files changed (high level):
- quickstarts/js-streaming-rag/README.md (new)
- quickstarts/js-streaming-rag/emulator/vectorstore-sim.js (new)
- quickstarts/js-streaming-rag/agent/streaming-agent.js (new)
- quickstarts/js-streaming-rag/agent/tools/url-fetcher.js (new)
- quickstarts/js-streaming-rag/test/e2e-emulator-smoke.js (new)
- quickstarts/js-streaming-rag/package.json (new)
- site/content/quickstarts/index.md (modified)
- .github/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml (modified, new job added)

Small illustrative snippets (kept intentionally tiny):
- streaming-agent.js shows using SDK stream API and handling partial tokens:
  const stream = client.responses.stream({ model: 'open-llm-like', input: prompt });
  for await (const chunk of stream) { process.stdout.write(chunk.text); }

- emulator API example:
  POST /ingest { documents: [{id: 'd1', text: '...'}], embedding_dim: 1536 }

Review conversation (condensed):
- Priya Nair: "Nice minimal flow. Suggest adding clear CORS/security note for the local emulator and require the emulator to default to localhost-only binding."
- Author (Asha): "Added a security note and bound emulator to 127.0.0.1 by default; documented how to override for CI. See commit 1c4a9b3."
- Diego Ramos: "E2E test looks good but flaked once on CI (timeout). Increase default timeouts for CI runner."
- Author: "Bumped timeouts and added retry in smoke script. See commit 9f0d7a8."
- Liam Chen: "Approved after quick lint fix and a brief mention in quickstarts index."

CI summary: quickstart-smoke (new job) initially failed on first run due to a flaky network timeout in GitHub Actions runner; rerun passed. Lint, build, and docs site link-checker all passed. The CI run added a new job to the quickstart workflow with node14/16 matrix for wider coverage.

Security notes: The vector-store emulator is explicitly labeled "for local development only" in the README. It listens only on 127.0.0.1 by default. The tools/url-fetcher includes a configured allowlist pattern and a timeout to reduce SSRF risk. No secrets are stored in the example.

Backward compatibility and breaking changes: none. This is additive content and no runtime or API surface of the platform is modified.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after approvals from Priya and Liam on 2026-02-26. CI green on final run.

How to try locally (short):
1) git checkout feature/js-rag-streaming-emulator-quickstart
2) cd quickstarts/js-streaming-rag && npm install
3) npm run start:emulator (starts on 127.0.0.1:7001)
4) npm run start:agent (starts example agent and connects to emulator)
notes: This PR intentionally keeps the emulator simple so teams can replicate retrieval + streaming behavior without external infra. For production guidance we add a link to the model-infra playbook in the README.
testing_instructions: Run npm run test:e2e in quickstarts/js-streaming-rag. CI job quickstart-smoke exercises start scripts and the smoke test. If you run locally, confirm emulator bound to 127.0.0.1 and set REDWOOD_API_KEY env to a test key or use the mocked mode in test config.
